paragraphs.source_en: The Mongol Century The Arrogance of Power: The Shahs of Khwarazm In the autumn of 1219 Chinggis Khan and a force of 150,000 Mongols and Uyghur Turks appeared suddenly beneath the high walls of Otrar on the Syr Darya near the southern border of present-day Kazakhstan. 1 After enduring a five-month siege, the defenders launched a desperate sally to break the Mongol ring. It failed and the Mongols killed all the warriors. Then the invaders drove all the civilians onto the plain, pillaged and burned the city, and put to the sword the entire population, estimated at 100,000. 2 Over the following three years, this grim process was repeated in most of the major cities of Central Asia, in Persia and the Middle East, and across modern Ukraine and Russia, clear to the borders of Poland (see plate 21).
